item.title: Elon Musk pledges to give a SpaceX share to every U.S. child
item.description: The SpaceX CEO wrote on social media on Monday that the gift "will be the first of many."

item.title: Feds probing suspicious letters to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators said they are looking into suspicious letters containing unknown substances that were mailed to state election officials and congressional offices.

item.title: Marco Rubio says there is "no pause" in intelligence sharing with Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claims that he received no early warning of a Russian attack from partner countries that previously shared intelligence, including the United States. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio responded, saying there's been no pause in intelligence-sharing. Katya Soldak, the editorial director of Forbes Media's international editions, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over waiving Russia sanctions
item.description: President Trump is defending his decision to waive sanctions, which will refill Russia's pocketbooks as it attacks Ukraine.

item.title: As AI dominates conversations, here are key terms to know
item.description: Artificial intelligence and the conversations around it are rapidly evolving. These terms can help to understand the developments.

item.title: Netanyahu tells Trump "we have a job to finish" on Iran
item.description: Russia's foreign minister is visiting Tehran for the first time since the U.S. and Israel launched their war with Iran.

item.title: 1 person killed in shooting near Columbus, Ohio, mosque
item.description: A shooting outside a mosque in Columbus, Ohio, was not an attack on the building and had nothing to do with it, police said.

item.title: Should you trust personal AI agents? What security experts say.
item.description: The more access you give personal AI agents, the more capable they can be. But should you trust them?

item.title: The quest to solve the mysterious fate of Amelia Earhart
item.description: A team of researchers went to Nikumaroro Island, a remote island in the Pacific Ocean, to search for Amelia Earhart's long-lost plane decades after she vanished. Here's a look at their expedition, the mysterious object that led them there and what comes next.

item.title: France vows to crack down after protests spiral out of control
item.description: French leaders call for local curfews and say an "ultra-left movement" was behind widespread violence and vandalism amid anti-government protests.

item.title: The AI doom scenario you've never heard of may be hardest to stop
item.description: The time to prepare for "gradual disempowerment" is now, according to researchers. One calls it "a civilization-scale problem."

item.title: Ex-OpenAI engineer who allegedly planted bug in office was in contact with Saudi royal family
item.description: A former OpenAI engineer who allegedly installed a listening device in an executive conference room was in close contact with a member of the Saudi royal family and was planning to leave the U.S. for Riyadh when authorities arrested him, federal prosecutors said Sunday in a court memorandum. CBS News' Nicole Sganga has more.

item.title: Musk pledges to give away one SpaceX share to every U.S. child
item.description: Elon Musk vowed in a social media post Monday to give one of his SpaceX shares to each child in the U.S. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent has more.

item.title: Starvation cult leader found guilty of murder of 190 children
item.description: Paul Mackenzie is alleged to have incited his acolytes to starve to death in order to "meet Jesus."

item.title: California billionaire tax could backfire, Stanford study says
item.description: A new analysis from Stanford economists cautions that enacting a billionaire tax could have unintended consequences.

item.title: Breaking down political turmoil in France as violent protests rage on
item.description: Protests continue to rage across France despite President Emmanuel Macron's attempts to mitigate the chaos. CBS News' Trevor Phillips has more.

item.title: Putin proposes summit with Trump and China's Xi to discuss Ukraine, Wall Street Journal reports
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin is proposing a summit with President Trump and China's Xi Jinping to discuss a potential end to the war in Ukraine, according to a report from the Wall Street Journal. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not been invited. Lingling Wei, chief China correspondent for the Wall Street Journal, joins to talk about her reporting and CBS News' Nancy Cordes has more from the White House.

item.title: What happens when you miss a debt payment — and how to recover fast
item.description: A missed debt payment can have lasting consequences, but how quickly you respond could make a big difference.

item.title: Why Alberta voters are weighing separating from Canada
item.description: Voters in Alberta are set to decide whether to hold a referendum to secede from Canada. Lisa Johnson, an Alberta legislature reporter for The Canadian Press, joins with more.

item.title: Trump launches women's health division within NIH alongside Melania Trump
item.description: President Trump is launching a new initiative alongside first lady Melania Trump to create a women's health division within the National Institutes of Health. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Trump heads to Kansas to rally Republicans; Vance's stunning response about Iran attack
item.description: President Trump is headed to Kansas to rally Republican voters ahead of the midterms. This comes as Vice President JD Vance also seeks GOP momentum for the November elections. Vance joined CBS News for a town hall. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Ex-OpenAI worker who allegedly planted bug contacted Saudi royal
item.description: The wife and infant son of the ex-OpenAI engineer left the U.S. for Saudi Arabia in October with business-class tickets purchased by a Saudi military official, prosecutors allege.

item.title: New evidence points to alleged O.J. Simpson accomplice in 1994 murders
item.description: A new investigation offers a different account of what might have happened the night O.J. Simpson's ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman were stabbed to death.

item.title: Trump signs executive order on women's health
item.description: "Who the hell wouldn't have a women's health division?" President Trump said Monday.

item.title: Supreme Court turns away appeal from alleged 9/11 mastermind
item.description: The Supreme Court rebuffed an effort by alleged 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed to revive a plea deal reached with military prosecutors and revoked by the Biden administration.

item.title: Expedition to find Amelia Earhart's missing plane comes up empty
item.description: The researchers said what they had hoped was the plane was "likely a collection of large trees" that had washed away, leaving a "single Y-shaped segment."

item.title: Air Force member dies in rappelling incident at UT San Antonio football game
item.description: A service member was injured and later died after falling while rappelling from the ceiling of the University of Texas at San Antonio football stadium on Saturday.

item.title: 7 highlights from JD Vance's CBS News town hall
item.description: In an hour-long town hall hosted by CBS News, Vice President JD Vance argued the Trump administration's handling of the economy and Iran will pay dividends in the future.

item.title: A Town Hall with JD Vance
item.description: Vice President JD Vance discusses ICE, the economy, corruption, midterms and more in this town hall moderated by Tony Dokoupil.

item.title: 10/17: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Pope Leo is cleared to leave the hospital after lung surgery, plus Albertans speak on the vote to potentially leave Canada. All this and more.
